subject: Re: Precision runway sizing & renewal amendment
messages:
From: Alex Ruiz <alex@greenlinelabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@greenlinelabs.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal sizing — sudden Q3 peak and ask for recommended add-ons

Vanessa,

Hope you’re well — quick note from our side. We just finished a post-mortem on last month’s surge. Baseline inference qps has increased ~2.5x for our chat ranking model and our latency p95 is creeping above our target during peak windows.

We start the formal renewal conversation next week, but before that procurement asked for a concrete sizing proposal and staged roll plan they can budget against. Can Redwood put together a recommended add (type + quantity), a short runway/thermal check plan, and a draft amendment (cost + expected latency SLOs) we can share with legal?

I attached a CSV with the usage slices we collected (Q3). If you need any additional telemetry let me know.

Thanks — would like to review something by 11/4 if possible.

— Alex
Alex Ruiz
Head of ML Engineering, Greenline Labs
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex@greenlinelabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal sizing — sudden Q3 peak and ask for recommended add-ons

Alex — thanks for the data and the heads up. I pulled the CSV into our capacity analyzer and looped in Karthik (SE) to propose a rightsize plan and Marissa for the commercial amendment.

Quick summary of what we see from the Q3 dump:
- Steady-state tokens/sec up ~2.5x, peak window duration ~30–40m/day
- Prefetch/KV cache hit is high on chat context but burst IO is driving extra warmup cost
- Current Dedicated pool: 48 x A100-40GB (shared across two services)

What I need from you to finalize the recommendation:
- Confirmation of upcoming traffic shaping (any planned model ensembles or new rerankers)
- Acceptable ramp cadence (immediate vs staged 2–6 weeks)

Deliverables we’ll send by 11/4:
1) A proposed sizing mix (device class + qty), expected throughput uplift, and cost delta.
2) A thermal-runway checklist (short test plan for your infra team, 1–2 days).
3) A draft amendment showing monthly committed GPUs and SLA targets; DocuSign link for review.

I attached a proposed-runway-sizing workbook and a short thermal-headroom-test-plan — draft only. Karthik: can you outline a staged onboarding (pilot -> canary -> full shift) with metrics to watch? Marissa: can you prepare a redlineable amendment with an option for a 2-week pilot credit?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
attachments: proposed-runway-sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet), thermal-headroom-test-plan.pdf (doc)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Alex Ruiz <alex@greenlinelabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal sizing — sudden Q3 peak and ask for recommended add-ons

Alex — ran the numbers against the current model profile and Q3 slices. High-level recommendation below; caveats afterward.

Recommended immediate staging (goal: reduce p95 latency and provide headroom without overspending):
- Pilot (2 weeks): +8 x H100-80GB in a dedicated burst pool (reserved short-term) to validate KV cache behavior under sustained peak.
- Canary (2–4 weeks): +16 x A100-80GB (mixed with existing A100-40GB) to smooth transition; use continuous batching and reduced prefill to test latency envelope.
- Full shift (post-canary): add remaining +24 x A100-80GB to reach net +48 effective A100-80GB-equivalent capacity (preserves throughput while improving memory headroom).

Estimated impact: p95 latency improvement ~20–35% in peak windows; sustained throughput uplift ~2.2–2.8x depending on batching.

Operational notes / thermal run checklist:
- Prioritize rolling restarts and KV cache warmup sequencing during pilot (we’ll provide a script).
- Observe per-GPU utilization and queuing; target utilization ceiling 65–75% during peak after canary.
- If tail latency persists, we can enable prefix-KV caching on the hottest endpoints and introduce a small LRU TTL.

Cost framing (ballpark monthly committed cost delta):
- Pilot burst pool (8 x H100 short-term) — credit possible; nominal engineering-to-prod carry cost.
- Committed add (48 x A100-80GB equivalent) — provided as a blended monthly rate in the amendment. Marissa will detail exact numbers and discount tiers.

I’ll attach the microbench outputs and a sample canary runbook in another note.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex@greenlinelabs.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Draft amendment + pilot credit for GL-3321

Alex — attached is a draft amendment summarizing the commercial terms for the proposed runway plan. Highlights:
- Two-week pilot credit (applies to up to 8 burst GPUs)
- Staged commit option: commit to baseline + phased tranches; pricing locked for 12 months for committed portion
- SLA: latency p95 objective for production route; credits tied to SLA breaches during committed period

DocuSign link: https://redwood.app/docusign/GL-3321-amendment
Drive with supporting numbers: https://drive.redwood.com/greenline/usage-q3

Please review and loop legal/procurement if this matches intent. Vanessa — feel free to redline pricing before I send for signatures.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
attachments: greenline-q3-usage.csv, proposed-runway-sizing.xlsx
From: Alex Ruiz <alex@greenlinelabs.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Draft amendment + pilot credit for GL-3321

Thanks team — this looks sensible and fast. Procurement has eyes on the DocuSign; legal will review the SLA language. We accept the two-week pilot approach and would like to start the pilot week of 11/15.

Can you confirm a single point-of-contact for the pilot kickoff and the expected pre-kickoff checklist so our infra team can reserve the window? Also confirm estimated go-live date if canary goes well (rough target: 12/06).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex
